name: Enzo Hins
tagline: I break things to learn how to defend them, and I build things because I like building.
degree: B.S. Computer Science, cybersecurity focus. Minors in Mathematics and Russian. May 2029.
about: I'm a sophomore at JMU studying computer science. I started on the defense side, running a Palo Alto firewall at MACCDC, and I keep getting pulled toward offense. Right now I lean red team, but I'm just as happy shipping a product.
I learn by entering competitions and writing down what went wrong afterward. The retrospectives under Writeups are the honest version, including the Splunk box we forgot to own.

Long term I want to do cyber work for national security, in defense or intelligence. Off the keyboard I train Brazilian jiu-jitsu, study Russian, and care about getting things right more than getting them fast.

quote.text: The things that we love tell us what we are.

now: Researching security for HGN-Sense at the Commonwealth Cyber Initiative
Leading infrastructure for the JMU Cyber Defense Club and running the Competitive Programming Club
Working through a 12-week C++ and reverse engineering plan (hexdump, PE/ELF parsing, Ghidra, pwn.college)
Studying for Security+ over winter break

experience.text: HGN-Sense uses ML to spot Horizontal Gaze Nystagmus eye movements and flag impairment for public safety. I'm the security person: AES-256-GCM encryption of subjects' biometric data, protection for the model weights, and anti-spoofing so the system can't be tricked.
Shipped AI search results and AI sticker and text generation to production on a greeting card platform, and researched local AI hosting.
Running a club of about 10 people.
Working with the university on cost-effective lab infrastructure for a club of about 25 members.
